rows.expectedResultText: Yellow or orange-yellow, crystalline, hygroscopic powder
Soluble in water, very slightly soluble in ethanol (96 per cent)
the spectrum obtained for the sample and compare to the spectrum obtained from riboflavin sodium phosphate CRS
A dense white precipitate is formed
The Sample is not more intensely colored than reference solution
The absorbance of the test solution is not greater than that of the reference solution

tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity. Hygroscopicity: weigh glass weighing vessel with stopper (m1); add about 2 g substance and weigh (m2); place un-stoppered in a climatic cabinet at 25 ± 1 °C for 24 h; stopper and weigh (m3); percentage increase in mass calculated (expression not given in the text). Very hygroscopic: increase >= 15 %; hygroscopic: 2 % to 15 %; slightly hygroscopic: < 2 %.

hygroscopicity.weighings: m1 vessel+stopper, m2 vessel+sample, m3 after 24 h
hygroscopicity.formula: not stated in the document (expression missing)

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake vigorously 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent).
IR identification (Test 1): mix intimately with potassium bromide, compress into a transparent pellet, compare the spectrum with that of riboflavin sodium phosphate CRS.

Reaction of sodium (Test 2): to 0.5 g add 10 mL nitric acid; evaporate to dryness; ignite residue until white; dissolve in 5 mL water; filter; take 2 mL of the filtrate, add 2 mL of 150 g/L potassium carbonate, heat to boiling (no precipitate is formed); add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution, heat to boiling, cool in iced water, rub the tube wall with a glass rod if necessary; a dense white precipitate is formed.

details.residueDissolvedIn: 5 mL water, filtered (filtrate reused for phosphate test)
details.intermediateCheck: no precipitate after potassium carbonate and boiling
details.potassiumAntimonateV: 4 mL; solution: 2 g potassium pyroantimonate in 95 mL hot water, cool quickly, add 2.5 g potassium hydroxide in 50 mL water + 1 mL dilute sodium hydroxide solution, stand 24 h, filter, dilute to 150 mL with water (STM line 26)

tests.procedure: Reaction of phosphate (Test 3): mix 1 mL of the filtrate from identification test 2 with 2 mL molybdovanadic reagent; a yellow colour develops.

details.molybdovanadicReagent: 4 g finely powdered ammonium molybdate + 0.1 g finely powdered ammonium vanadate, 70 mL water, grind, add 20 mL nitric acid, dilute to 100 mL with water (STM line 26)

tests.procedure: Dissolve 0.5 g in carbon dioxide-free water, dilute to 50 mL with the same solvent; measure with a calibrated pH meter.
Dissolve 0.300 g in 18.2 mL hydrochloric acid R1 and dilute to 25.0 mL with water; measure specific optical rotation (polarimeter); result on dried substance.

details.solvent: 18.2 mL hydrochloric acid R1, dilute to 25.0 mL with water
details.hydrochloricAcidR1: 70 g hydrochloric acid diluted to 100 mL with water (STM line 26)

tests.procedure: Impurity E: to about 35 mg add 10 mL methylene chloride, shake 5 min, filter; the filtrate is not more intensely coloured than reference solution BY6.

details.referenceSolution: BY6: 5.0 mL standard solution BY + 95.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.standardSolutionBY: 2.4 mL yellow solution + 1.0 mL red solution + 0.4 mL blue solution + 6.2 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)
details.yellowSolution: 46 g ferric chloride in about 900 mL of (25 mL HCl + 975 mL water), to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture
details.redSolution: 60 g cobalt chloride in about 900 mL of (25 mL HCl + 975 mL water), to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture
details.blueSolution: 'Blue primary solution': 63 g copper sulfate pentahydrate in about 900 mL of (25 mL HCl + 975 mL water), to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture

tests.procedure: Inorganic phosphate: test solution 0.150 g in water to 50 mL; to 10.0 mL add 10.0 mL acid molybdate solution and 5.0 mL ferrous sulfate solution, mix. Reference: solution containing KH2PO4 equivalent to 0.440 g in 1000 mL, diluted with water to 10 times its volume immediately before use; to 10.0 mL add 10.0 mL acid molybdate solution and 5.0 mL ferrous sulfate solution, mix. Measure absorbance of both at 700 nm using water as compensation liquid; test absorbance must not exceed the reference.

details.testSolution: 0.150 g in water to 50 mL; 10.0 mL + 10.0 mL acid molybdate solution + 5.0 mL ferrous sulfate solution
details.referenceSolution: KH2PO4 equivalent to 0.440 g/1000 mL diluted to 10 times its volume with water (immediately before use); 10.0 mL + 10.0 mL acid molybdate solution + 5.0 mL ferrous sulfate solution
details.criterion: absorbance of test solution not greater than that of reference solution

tests.procedure: Weigh empty weighing bottle (previously dried at 105 °C, cooled in desiccator) W0; weigh accurately 1.000 g into it, W1 = bottle + material; dry in calibrated oven at 105 °C for 5 h, cool in desiccator, weigh W2; repeat to constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

Assay (UV): dissolve 0.100 g in 150 mL water, add 2 mL glacial acetic acid, dilute to 1000.0 mL with water; to 10.0 mL add 3.5 mL of 14 g/L sodium acetate solution and dilute to 50.0 mL with water; measure absorbance at the maximum at 444 nm; content of C17H20N4O6 with specific absorbance 328. % Assay = Abs x 1000 x 50 x 100 / (Wt x S.A x 10 x (100 - LOD)).

details.dissolution: 150 mL water + 2 mL glacial acetic acid, dilute to 1000.0 mL with water
details.aliquot: 10.0 mL + 3.5 mL of 14 g/L sodium acetate solution, dilute to 50.0 mL with water
details.formula: % Assay = (Abs x 1000 x 50 x 100) / (Wt x S.A x 10 x (100 - LOD)); Abs = absorbance, Wt = sample weight (g), S.A = 328, LOD = loss on drying (%)
details.storageNote: preserve in an airtight container, protected from light (STM line 24)

notApplicable.justification: major and minor components not available

openQuestions.question: Minimum quantity: spec sheet says '200 ml' (unit ml, not g); STM says 50 g for routine testing and retention and 25 g for periodic retesting. User answer 200 g applied to routine; retest kept at the STM's 25 g. Confirm the retest quantity (and that retention is no longer 50 g).
Hygroscopicity (part of Appearance): the expression for the percentage increase in mass is missing from the text (m1, m2, m3 defined, no formula). No formula transcribed.
Specific optical rotation: no instrument conditions (wavelength, temperature, tube length), no calculation formula, and no unit are given; spec is on the dried substance. Row has no unit.
Inorganic phosphate: 'acid molybdate solution' and 'ferrous sulfate solution' are used but not defined in the STM reagent list (ferrous sulfate is not in the Materials list either).

Inorganic phosphate: the reference-solution wording 'potassium dihydrogen phosphate equivalent to 0.440 g of KH2PO4 in 1000 ml' is as written; confirm it means 0.440 g KH2PO4 per 1000 mL. Spec row is a comparison (no numeric limit).
Assay: compensation liquid (blank) and cell path length are not stated.

Identification IR spec text is incomplete as written ('the spectrum obtained for the sample and compare to the spectrum obtained from ... CRS', no 'corresponds/concordant'); row kept with the sheet's wording.

Document control mismatch: spec sheet is version 1/0, issued 15-05-2024, header code VB010121800065 with related codes VB010121800062, VB010100100021; STM is version 1/1 (issue date blank); STM history reads 'STM-SM-56' for the code; STM name is 'Riboflavin Sodium Phosphate', sheet item name 'Riboflavin 5-phosphate'. itemName follows the spec sheet.
Impurity E colour reference: STM lists 'Blue Solution' in standard solution BY, but only 'Blue primary solution' is defined; assumed the same.
